query_text: Tell me about some weird habits that some people have.

message.content:
Based on my search, here are some weird and unusual habits that people have:

## Everyday Quirks

**Thanking Inanimate Objects**
Some people have the habit of whispering "thank you" to objects when they're done using them—like saying goodbye to a phone when putting it down, or thanking a microwave after heating food. One person even says goodbye to their apartment when leaving for vacation, explaining that they'll be back soon "just in case it misses me."

**Eating Habits**
- Eating meals in reverse order of desirability—saving the best for last and never mixing foods
- Eating cereal with a fork to avoid soggy pieces
- Eating entire apples (except the stem) and strawberries with the leaves still on
- Needing to see food clearly before eating—refusing to eat in the dark and needing to know candy colors

**Compulsive Ratios**
When eating cheese and crackers, some people obsessively try to maintain a perfect 1:1 ratio so they end with exactly one slice of cheese and one cracker left.

## Socially Awkward Behaviors

**Overthinking Greetings**
Socially awkward people may rehearse simple greetings like "hello" multiple times before an interaction, analyzing whether a handshake, nod, or smile is appropriate—then continue analyzing the interaction long after it ends.

**Mental Scripting**
Some people rely on pre-prepared "scripts" for social situations like ordering coffee or making small talk at parties, treating everyday conversations like theatrical performances that require rehearsal.

**Hyper-Focus on Interests**
Socially awkward individuals often become deeply absorbed in specific hobbies or topics, sometimes to the point of appearing obsessive, and may eagerly share extensive knowledge without realizing others may not share the same enthusiasm.

## Historical Genius Habits

**Nikola Tesla's Toe Exercises**
Tesla would tightly curl and uncurl his toes 100 times for each foot every night, claiming it stimulated his brain cells. He also reportedly slept less than two hours nightly and eventually stopped eating solid food entirely, consuming only a vegetable-based "health potion" he concocted.

**Igor Stravinsky's Headstands**
The composer did headstands as part of his daily routine, claiming they "rested his head and cleared his brain." He also incorporated sunbathing into his schedule for health benefits.

**Albert Einstein's Empty Pipe**
Even after his doctor ordered him to stop smoking, Einstein continued to hold an empty pipe in his mouth and chew on it.

## Modern Unusual Routines

**ASMR Relaxation**
Millions of people now use ASMR (Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response) videos featuring gentle sounds as a primary relaxation method—a habit that would have seemed bizarre just a decade ago.

**Scent Collections**
Some people collect smells as "sensory memories"—gathering soil from different countries, preserving the smell of old books, or keeping worn clothing specifically for their scent.

**Mouth Taping for Sleep**
Influencer Ashton Hall went viral for taping his mouth shut while sleeping as part of his extreme 3:52 a.m. morning routine, which also includes plunging his face in cold water and eating breakfast standing at his desk.

## Memory Tricks

**Phantom Writing**
To remember something short-term, some people mimic the motion of writing on a notepad by scribbling their right index finger on their left palm—creating a physical memory without any actual writing.

**Menu Browsing as Entertainment**
Some people browse restaurant menus online for fun even when they have no intention of visiting, or read Google Maps reviews of specific restaurant chains they've never been to (one person admitted to being fascinated with Olive Garden reviews despite never having eaten there).

---

These habits range from charmingly eccentric to genuinely unusual, but psychologists note that some degree of "weirdness" is normal and may even be a way to preserve individuality. As one article notes: "If a behavior doesn't harm anyone, coexists peacefully with others, and serves as a way for someone to express themselves—why call it strange?"

2. https://www.amraandelma.com/influencers-with-unusual-daily-routines/
3. https://www.bolde.com/socially-awkward-people-do-15-weird-things/
4. https://www.buzzfeed.com/ravenishak/habits-that-others-find-weird-reddit
5. https://shefeq.com/en/strange-habits-the-daily-routines-of-the-worlds-most-unusual-people/683
